podcast.title: Four-Song Cassette (1989)
podcast.body: Bad Radio released a four-song cassette in 1989, which hinted at more music to come. This release occurred during Eddie Vedder's tenure as their singer, shortly before he departed to join Pearl Jam. "There was a four-song cassette released in 1989. That hinted of more to come."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Disintegration After Eddie Vedder's Departure
podcast.body: Bad Radio, a funk-rock band fronted by Eddie Vedder from 1986 to 1990, continued for a short period after Vedder left in February 1990 to join what would become Pearl Jam. The band eventually disintegrated following his departure, with their planned album remaining unreleased. "Bad Radio continued for a while, but eventually disintegrated."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Duran Duran Inspiration
podcast.body: Before Eddie Vedder joined, Bad Radio's primary musical inspiration was Duran Duran, a sound that the band found wasn't working for them. "Before Eddie joined, the band's main inspiration was Durand Durand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pearl Jam Fan Community Bootlegs
podcast.body: Despite their unreleased album, the Pearl Jam fan community has actively kept Bad Radio's music alive by circulating bootlegs of their material. This effort by fans ensures that the music from Eddie Vedder's pre-Pearl Jam band remains accessible. "Meanwhile, the Pearl Jam fan community has kept Bad Radio alive by circulating boot legs of Bad Radio stuff."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Red Hot Chili Peppers Sound Shift
podcast.body: After Eddie Vedder became their singer, Bad Radio's sound evolved to become increasingly similar to that of the Red Hot Chili Peppers. "After Eddie came on board, Bad Radio began to sound more and more like the Red Hot Chili Peppers."

xref.title: Joining Bad Radio
xref.body: Eddie Vedder secured his position as singer for Bad Radio largely due to a homemade demo where he covered Bruce Springsteen's "Atlantic City." The band had been inspired by Duran Duran but sought a new singer, leading to auditions where Eddie was chosen. "Eddie got the gig. And largely because they liked his homemade demo of him covering Bruce Springsteen's Atlantic City."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Pre-Pearl Jam Jobs and Bands
xref.body: Before moving from San Diego to Seattle to join Pearl Jam, Eddie Vedder moved from Chicago to San Diego where he worked booking bands in a club, security at a hotel, and at a gas station, alongside his passion for surfing. He was involved in several bands, including The Butts, Surf and Destroy, and Indian Style (featuring future Rage Against the Machine drummer Brad Wilk), with Bad Radio showing the most promise. "When Eddie Vetter moved from Chicago to San Diego, he got a job booking bands in a club. He also worked security at a hotel. He worked at a gas station and he spent a lot of time surfing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Severe Stage Fright
xref.body: While in Bad Radio, Eddie Vedder suffered from severe stage fright, to the extent that he sometimes wore goggles that were blocked out or "blinders" so he couldn't see the audience. "Eddie had severe stage fright. And sometimes had to wear goggles that were blocked out so he couldn't see the audience."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
